articleTitle: Strong stabilization of neutral functional differential equations
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: A linear neutral functional differential equation is called strongly exponentially stable if it is exponentially stable when subjected to small variations in the delays. In this paper we present necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a feedback control so that the resulting closed‐loop neutral functional differential equation is strongly exponentially stable.

articleTitle: Oscillations in lossless propagation models: a Liapunov–Krasovskii approach
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: This paper focuses on Forced oscillations (periodic and almost periodic) in some dynamical models described by coupled differential and difference equations. The existence and stability result is based on a theorem on invariant manifolds on Banach spaces due to Kurzweil and Halanay. The state‐space (based on Liapunov–Krasovskii functionals combined with the S‐procedure) approach is considered. An illustrative example is presented and some conclusions are drawn concerning sharpness and ease in applications of the method.

articleTitle: H∞ control of system with I/O delay: a review of some problem‐oriented methods
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: Systems with input or output delays form the simplest, and yet one of the most widely applied classes of distributed parameter models. This is a review of some problem‐oriented H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> methods for that class, with an emphasis on computational simplicity. Reviewed methods include operator interpolation, game‐theoretic state‐space treatments in the time domain, a J‐spectral factorization approach, and methods exploiting various ideas from sampled‐data theory. Some interesting properties of the (sub) optimal solution are discussed as well.

articleTitle: Sliding mode control of linear time delay systems: a design via LMIs
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: Two types of sliding mode controllers for uncertain time delay system are designed. The conditions for the existence of the sliding regime are studied via Lyapunov–Krasovskii functionals. The upper bound of the delay is then shown to be the solution of a convex minimization problem expressed in terms of LMIs. A third‐order example illustrates the design methods.

articleTitle: Stability of systems with state‐dependent and random delays
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: The Lyapunov–Krasovskii theory is extended to systems with varying delay time. First we consider stochastic delay times, and derive sufficient conditions for stochastic global asymptotic stability. These conditions are of the ‘standard’ Riccati equation form, together with a bound on the expected rate of change of the time delay. Next we establish some results for the asymptotic stability of systems with state‐dependent delay.

articleTitle: Identifiability analysis of linear delay‐differential systems
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: In this paper, identification of linear delay‐differential systems is studied. The components of the state are assumed to be available whereas system parameters including system and input delays are unknown. Such a system is shown to be identifiable if and only if it is weakly controllable. If the weak controllability condition is satisfied the corresponding identification problem admits a unique solution while a sufficiently rich system input is applied. Construction of sufficiently rich input signals independent of any underlying system completes the fully practical framework for parameter identifiability of linear delay differential systems.

articleTitle: Neutral‐type time‐delay systems that are not formally stable are not BIBO stabilizable
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: It is shown that a time‐delay system of neutral type that is not formally stable cannot be stabilized, in the sense of bounded input bounded output (BIBO) Stabilization, by any feedback in the large class of distributed systems that are Laplace transformable, even using derivatives in the control law. As a result, a time‐delay system of neutral type is BIBO stabilizable if and only if it is formally stable and spectrally stabilizable.

articleTitle: Non‐uniform stabilization of control systems
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: Aversion of non‐uniform in time robust global asymptotic stability is proposed and enables us to derive: (1) sufficient conditions for the stabilization of uncertain nonlinear triangular time‐varying control systems; (2) sufficient conditions for the solution of the partial‐state global stabilization problem for autonomous systems. The results are obtained via the method of integrator backstepping and are generalizations of the existing corresponding results in the literature.

articleTitle: Nonlinear delay systems, Lie algebras and Lyapunov transformations
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: In this paper we consider nonlinear delay systems of the form x (t) = A(x(t), x(t – δ))x(t) + B(x(t), x(t – δ))u(t) and obtain new stability and control results by replacing the system by a sequence of linear, time‐varying systems and using an explicit representation for the solution of such systems in terms of a Lie algebra associated with the system. In the case of nilpotent Lie algebras we use a Lyapunov transformation to prove stability.

articleTitle: The influence of delays when averaging slow and fast oscillating systems: overview
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: This paper presents an overview of results in averaging theory. First, averaging for ordinary differential equations (ODEs) is presented. These results are then applied to fast oscillating differential equations to show how zero average perturbations can affect stability properties. Next, averaging for functional differential equations (FDEs) is presented. A comparison of ‘classical’ averaged models and more recently developed averaged models for FDEs is given. Then the FDE averaging results are applied to fast oscillating delay differential equations. It is explained that fast oscillating FDEs are often sensitive to extremely small delays. Several examples are presented in this paper to help give an overview of results.

articleTitle: Robust stability of a class of linear time‐varying systems
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: This paper firstly considers the exponential stability of unforced linear systems of slowly time‐varying dynamics. Possible switchings of the system structure to unstable dynamics during certain finite time intervals are admitted. The maintenance of global exponential stability does not necessarily require at most a finite number of switchings in the dynamics while infinitely many switches can also lead to stability. The mechanism to achieve stability under infinitely many switches in the dynamics is to maintain the system in the stable region during time intervals of sufficiently large length without switches provided that the system dynamics evolves at a sufficiently small rate with time. Special attention is paid to the robust tolerance to a class of state disturbances and to the case of a time‐varying matrix of dynamics that possess either piecewise constant or constant eigenvalues. The obtained results can be relevant for their use in stability issues for the cases of multimodel non‐adaptive and adaptive control with improved transient performances.

articleTitle: Control of delay systems with relay
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: We study the periodic oscillations of a first‐order delayed linear system with relay output and proportional + integral feedback and describe the behaviour of the general solutions of the closed loop. For the system under study, we first exhibit a countable set of periodic limit cycles. We show that in the particular case where only proportional control is used, any solution tends in finite time towards one of the limit cycles (whose determination depends on the initial conditions). All the cycles are orbitally unstable except one of them, the only slowly oscillating one. We provide exact computations of their period and amplitude. We then show how these results may be used to identify the parameters of the plant and to tune the control‐law parameters in order to control the amplitude and the period of the slowly oscillating limit cycle. Finally, we provide some well‐posedness and ultimate boundedness results for a time‐varying perturbed version of the system under study. The given estimates show that the proportional + integral feedback law permits rejection of various parametric perturbations.

articleTitle: Adaptive servomechanism design for boundary control systems
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: In this paper we consider the design of adaptive servomechanism for boundary control systems in the case of the input and output operators being collocated. An adaptive servomechanism is constructed by the concept of high‐gain output feedback and the estimation mechanism of the unknown parameters for the bounded disturbances. Moreover, a controller is designed to be inverse optimal. It minimizes a meaningful cost functional that incorporates integral penalty on the tracking error state, the control and the parameter error.

articleTitle: An analytical theory for Riemannian cubic polynomials
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: We establish some global existence and multiplicity results for Riemannian cubic polynomials in a complete Riemannian manifold.

articleTitle: Robust H∞ control of uncertain systems with time‐varying state and control input delays
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: In this paper, a new method for robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> controller of uncertain systems with time‐varying state and control input delays is proposed. A sufficient condition, which is dependent on the maximum value of the time derivative of time‐varying delay, is also presented for the existence of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> controller. The proposed controller not only stabilizes closed‐loop uncertain systems but also guarantees a prescribed H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> norm bound of the closed‐loop transfer matrix from the disturbance to controlled output. Furthermore, we propose a new robust stability criterion to decide the allowed maximum bound of plant uncertainty which still can be stabilized by proposed robust controller. An example given illustrates the availability of the proposed design method.

articleTitle: Functional controllability and right invertibility for systems over rings
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: This paper is devoted to study the structure of linear systems with coefficients in a ring in connection with the so‐called functional controllability property and the right inversion problem. A geometric characterization of functional controllability is given and a related notion of relative degree is introduced. Applications to delay‐differential systems are considered.

articleTitle: On controllability of semilinear stochastic systems in Hilbert spaces
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: The Nussbaum fixed‐point theorem together with conditions for approximate controllability of linear systems are used to obtain sufficient conditions for approximate controllability of associated semilinear stochastic systems in Hilbert spaces.

articleTitle: Minimal bases of matrix pencils and coprime matrix fraction descriptions
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: Two new methods for the construction of coprime MFDs are proposed starting from a minimal state space realization of a transfer function matrix. The approaches are based on the construction of minimal bases for the kernels of the state‐space‐based pencils [s I − A, − B], [s I − A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sup>, −C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sup>]. The latter problem is explicitly solved using the Toeplitz matrix construction of minimal bases of matrix pencils. The numerical algorithms of the methods are presented and some examples demonstrating the implementation of the algorithms are also given.

articleTitle: Output feedback design for uncertain systems with delays
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: This paper develops a robust scheme for output feedback design of a class of uncertain systems with input as well as state delays. The delay factors are unknown and time‐invariant and the parametric uncertainties are norm‐bounded. By employing a Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional approach, it is proven that the closed‐loop controlled system is asymptotically stable independent of the delay factors. The observer and state feedback controller gains are determined by solving two linear matrix inequalities which are independent of the size of the delay factors. A simulation example is given to illustrate the theoretical developments.

articleTitle: Sliding mode control of uncertain systems: a singular perturbation approach
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: In this paper we consider a nonlinear control system affected by deterministic uncertainty and described by a system of ordinary differential equations. The uncertainty is modelled by a multivalued map whose t‐measurable and x‐Lipschitz selections represent the possible system dynamics of the uncertain system. We propose a dynamical feedback control design, based on the singular perturbation theory, which allows all the possible system trajectories corresponding to the system dynamics to have the same prescribed behaviour. Specifically, given a manifold K of the state space, defined as the zeros of a smooth map, the proposed control steers and then holds, during finite or infinite time intervals, any possible system trajectory to any prescribed neighbourhood of K. A result ensuring the exact attainability of K is also provided. Some examples illustrating the obtained results are presented.

articleTitle: L‐splines—a manifestation of optimal control
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: We show connections between L‐splines and optimal control theory, leading to the conclusion that L‐splines are manifestations of an optimal behaviour.

articleTitle: A trajectory interpretation of torsion‐free controllability
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information

articleTitle: Control of an interconnected power system: a time delay approach
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: This paper investigates the control problem of a large interconnected power systems in the presence of measurement delays. A remote output feedback controller is designed in order to stabilize the power system and to improve the damping of low‐frequency inter‐area oscillations. Sufficient conditions for closed‐loop stability, functions of the input delay are given in terms of the existence of symmetric and positive definite solutions of linear matrix inequalities. Time‐domain simulations, performed on a realistic nonlinear model (29‐machine, 400 states) show the robustness of the proposed control law during severe events such as short‐circuits or sudden large variations of load.

articleTitle: Finite‐dimensional H∞ control of flexible beam equation systems
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: In this paper, we consider H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> control problem with measurement feedback for flexible beam equation systems. The aim is to construct a finite‐dimensional H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> controller with a given level δ for the flexible beam equation system. For that purpose, we first formulate the system as an infinite‐dimensional system in l<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and derive a finite‐dimensional reduced‐order system for the infinite‐dimensional system. Then, an H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> controller with level d less than δ is constructed for the reduced‐order model. The finite‐dimensional controller together with a residual mode filter plays a role of a finite‐dimensional H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> controller with level δ for the original flexible beam equation system, if the order of the residual mode filter is chosen sufficiently large.

articleTitle: New algorithm to construct a stabilizing controller for linear systems over integral domains
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: We are concerned with the coordinate‐free approach to control systems, which is a factorization approach but does not require the coprime factorizations of plants, provided only that the set of stable causal transfer functions forms an integral domain. We first present a new criterion of the feedback stabilizability. This is a generalization of the criteria in terms of reduced minors given by Sule in 1994 and in terms of quotient ideals given by Shankar and Sule in 1992. We then present an algorithm to construct a stabilizing controller, which is derived from the result given by Lin in 1998. Sule's algorithm and its derivations need to convert some matrices over some ring of fractions to ones over the set of stable causal transfer functions, which may raise the unnecessarily complicated calculations. On the other hand, the algorithm of this paper does not require such a conversion. An illustrative example to construct a stabilizing controller is also presented.

articleTitle: Guest editorial introduction to the special issue on analysis and design of delay and propagation systems
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information

articleTitle: Mean‐square filtering problem in hereditary systems with nonzero initial conditions
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: The optimal mean‐square filtering problem for linear hereditary dynamic systems with nonzero initial conditions is considered. In contrast to the resolved classical problem with zero initial conditions, the filtering problem under consideration reduces to a non‐classical linear‐quadratic optimal problem. The solution of the latter problem is unknown. We replace this non‐classical problem by a simplified classical one, which has a known solution. The solution of this approximate problem is used instead of the solution for the exact original problem. By applying the duality theory we obtain an estimate for the nonoptimality level of the simplified solution. It is essential that this estimate can be computed without exactly solving the initial complex filtering problem.

articleTitle: Optimal control of parabolic equation with an infinite number of variables for non‐standard functional and time delay
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: A distributed control problem for the parabolic operator with an infinite number of variables and time delay is considered. The performance index has an integral form. Constraints on controls are imposed. To obtain optimality conditions for the Neumann problem, the generalization of the Dubovitskii–Milyutin theorem given by Walczak in WALCZAK, S. Folia Mathematics, 1, 187–196 and WALCZAK, S. J. Optim. Theory Appl., 42, 561–582 was applied.

Author Keywords: parabolic operators with an infinite number of variables with time delay

articleTitle: Multiplicative groups used for coding QAM signals
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: Recently, some multiplicative groups of algebraic integers were used to obtain quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) signal spaces and to design error‐correcting codes. This paper shows that one subgroup of the multiplicative group of units in the algebraic integer ring of each quadratic number field with unique factorization property Q(√m), modulo the ideal (2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>), can be used to obtain a QAM signal space of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n–2</sup> points with good geometrical properties, where n ≥ 3, m ≢ 1 (mod 8) and m is a square‐free rational integer. These QAM signals can be coded such that a differentially coherent method can be applied to demodulate the QAM signals. The multiplicative subgroups can also be used to construct block codes over Gaussian integers which are able to correct some error patterns.

articleTitle: On a dynamical identification of controls in nonlinear time‐lag systems
publicationTitle: IMA Journal of Mathematical Control and Information
abstract: We study the problem of dynamical identification of unknown inputs (disturbances, or sometimes control) to nonlinear systems described by differential equations with delays. We use an approach based on the construction of a feedback control which should act on a suitable ‘model’ of the given system. The state of the model system is then compared with that of the plant, at discrete time instants. We shall obtain in this way enough information for the construction of a sequence of feedback controls v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> (·), which approximate the unknown input.
